pillar_reactions.evidence: Mobility is why he took the call — 'it seems like you guys are incorporating more mobility into your routines' — and he volunteered belief in the modality unprompted: 'I'm a believer in the kettlebells. I am. And I'm a believer that it's not about going to the gym and just pulling on the lat machine.' He also endorsed the efficiency framing before the rep offered it.

The rep conceded the pillar was largely unnecessary for him — 'it sounds like you're doing pretty good on the nutrition part, sure, I'm sure there could be 5% optimization in it' — after the prospect described four to five months of whole-food discipline and roughly four cheat meals in four months. No pushback and no questions.

Interrogated the mechanics closely rather than reacting to the value: 'you're given, what I'm assuming, probably four workouts a week kind of thing?', 'after the workout, what am I downloading?', 'which app', 'is there a weekly check-in with Trevor, is that what I just heard', 'so check-ins really done then through like a text?'. Understanding the delivery model, not buying into it — and his verdict at the end was 'pretty darn similar to what I just did'.

anchors.raw: it was a couple thousand bucks if I remember it
anchors.note: Roughly $500 a month against $1,000 a month, and it delivered 20 lb of weight loss and a fall from about 20% to 13% body fat. The rep asked for this number and then never used it. This is the anchor that will decide the deal in a month's time.

anchors.raw: certainly the kettlebell program I'm on, they want me to continue
anchors.note: An active competitor with an existing relationship, a track record with this specific prospect, and five weeks of exclusive access in which to make a renewal offer — during which Primal has no contract, no onboarding and no next call booked.

anchors.raw: there's part of me that says, you're, you're in this far enough that you can, that you can do it on your own
anchors.note: He has already proven a free fallback works — when his back forced a layoff he improvised dips and pull-ups and 'I'm seeing progress from that, too'. The zero-cost option is credible to him and was never challenged.

anchors.raw: there's another piece of me that knows this, a little bit of structure and accountability, I do better
anchors.note: He gave the buying reason himself in the same sentence as the objection, and it went unquoted back to him. Combined with a demonstrated willingness to pay for coaching, capacity and belief are both present.

unmet_demand.want: Frequent, close attention to form — the single thing he named as missing, having received feedback roughly once a month
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Partly served and partly unproven. The rep described daily video review in month one, which is exactly the answer, but said nothing about what form attention looks like in months two to six — which is precisely where the incumbent's monthly cadence failed him. Nobody asked and nobody stated it.

unmet_demand.want: To feel athletic rather than stiff after high-volume swinging
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The mobility pillar was presented and is plausibly the right answer, but no mechanism was described for diagnosing or reversing existing swing-induced stiffness beyond 'give Trevor a big list of everything going on'. The claim was asserted rather than demonstrated to a prospect who has already been disappointed by one programme's mobility content.

unmet_demand.want: A shorter commitment reflecting that he is not starting cold — 'I could also make the argument that I'm not coming into this thing fully cold'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: A three-month tier at $4,000 was quoted, so the want was met — but at a price outside the sanctioned structure and without the guarantee, which was stated as attaching to the six-month only. The programme has no differentiated offer for an experienced intake versus a beginner beyond a shorter clock.
